title: The Beetles That Doubled Backward
story: In the abandoned moonstone mine, Veskalune's gloombeetles pour from a crack in the wall and double in number every single hour. Five hours after dusk, Mr 6 counts 192 of them glowing on the ceiling. The sealing rune on the crack only works if he carves the exact number that crawled out at dusk — so Mr 6 sits down and thinks backward.
question: How many gloombeetles crawled out of the crack at dusk?
solution: Doubling five times multiplies the start by 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 32.
praise: Undoing the doubling by dividing was exactly the right plan — it just needs to be undone once for every hour, all five times.
hint: If the brood doubled once each hour for five hours, how many times must you halve 192 to travel back to dusk?
victory: Mr 6 carved a glowing 6 on the crack — his own favorite number — and the whole brood folded neatly back inside like a closing fan. 'Six,' he said, dusting his cape. 'I'd know it anywhere.'
imagePrompt: A ceiling of hundreds of softly glowing green beetles in a dark moonstone mine, with a small caped numeral 6 knight kneeling on the floor scratching numbers in the dust by lantern light.
